data: First European Moon mission — solar-electric ion drive. Spiralled to the Moon over 13 months; deliberate impact 2006-09-03

ESA's first lunar mission and the first European spacecraft to reach the Moon. SMART = Small Missions for Advanced Research in Technology — and the technology that mattered was a Hall-effect solar-electric ion thruster (PPS-1350, the largest such thruster flown at the time). Launched 2003-09-27 as a shared payload on an Ariane 5 from Kourou, the 367-kg spacecraft used its 1.2-kW xenon ion drive over 13 months to slowly raise its Earth orbit, eventually captured by lunar gravity 2004-11-15. Operated for about 22 months in a polar lunar orbit, returning high-resolution AMIE camera imagery, X-ray fluorescence elemental maps of the Moon (D-CIXS), and infrared mineral spectroscopy (SIR). Deliberately impacted Lacus Excellentiae (34.4° S, 46.2° W) on 2006-09-03 05:42 UTC — the impact flash was observed from the Canada-France-Hawaii Telescope.
First European spacecraft to reach the Moon; first mission to reach the Moon under ion propulsion
ESA's first Mars orbiter; Europe's first planetary mission
First spacecraft to orbit a comet (67P)
First close-up images of a cometary nucleus — flew 596 km past Halley's Comet at 68 km/s in 1986
ESA flagship to Jupiter — first orbiter ever to settle around a Galilean moon (Ganymede, 2034)
First asteroid sample ever returned to Earth

ESA's first lunar mission. Used solar-electric (ion) propulsion to spiral out from a geostationary transfer orbit to lunar capture — a 14-month, fuel-efficient transit that pioneered low-thrust trajectories for ESA's later interplanetary missions. Deliberately impacted the lunar surface in 2006 for an observed end-of-life experiment.
